infos.prompt: Why do the heirs hold you?
lines: I killed a man of the heirs. He had sold my sister's Owing on to the crossings, and I do not deny what I did.
By our law a killing is worked off for the dead man's household. I work it for them as it is owed, and I do not ask you to call it small.
The two beside me have their own reasons. Ask them.
Then I go once Tsaxi has turned his back.
Go back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house. Tell Never-Sold the name Hides-In-Reeds, and that I came out.

infos.prompt: Tsaxi will let one of the others go.
lines: Then that is the right of it. I killed. The heirs hold me for it. It sits hard to be the one who is left, but I do not ask to be chosen.
Whoever goes out should take the name to Never-Sold, in her house on the far side of the town.
I am still here. I do not blame you for it. One went out and I did not. I would have chosen the same.
I killed and the heirs hold me for it. That has not changed.

infos.prompt: Why do the heirs hold you?
lines: I came to the Rose with nowhere else to go, the season my daughter was taken onto the estate. The heirs gave me a place by their fire. I ate what they gave me and was glad of it.
They have counted that shelter ever since. The count is larger with each season. When I die, the heirs will look to my daughter for what I ate. That is a debt she never sat down to.

I will not tell you mine is the better case. The two beside me were held for what they did or said, and I am old, with fewer years to give. I have not seen my daughter since the season she was taken, and I would see her again.
Then I walk out when Tsaxi looks away. I did not look for it. I will not say I earned it more than the two that I leave behind.
Give my name to Never-Sold: Keeps-The-Old-Count. Let her hear that it was I who walked out alive.
The way back is north-west through Blackrose, to the Chainbreakers' house. When I am free of this shore, I will go looking for my daughter.

infos.prompt: Tsaxi will let one of the others go.
lines: Then one of the others walks out. I keep my place here. I am old. I have only my years to give the heirs, so I will go on giving them.
I ask one thing of you. If you meet my daughter, do not tell her I am still held. She would try to carry my count. The heirs would let her.
Never-Sold keeps the Chainbreakers' house. Go back to her, north-west across the town.
I am still here at the heirs' post. One of us has gone out, and the one beside me stays. I would sooner it was a younger case that was answered.
If you have any word of my daughter, Rows-For-Another, good or bad, I would take it. I ask only that she is not told where I am.

There is. A fire went through Blackrose Prison, which the families born there call the Rose. The heirs of those families brought three held there out of the smoke. They keep them at their stone house on the east shore of Blackrose.

The three are Says-It-Plain, Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count, who is Rows-For-Another's mother. The keeper, Third-Born Tsaxi, might count one of them lost to the smoke for good words or for coin, I think. Here are a hundred gold for him. They are yours to keep if words do the work.

From here go south-east through Blackrose to the shore. The stone house stands at the water's edge. Tsaxi stands outside its west wall, on the town side. I will not say which one should go. Hear all three first. They stand with him by the stone house.
I have nothing more for you yet. Come back when the first matter is closed.
The stone house is on the east shore, south-east through Blackrose from here. Tsaxi stands outside its west wall, on the town side. Hear all three before you choose.

Says-It-Plain goes, then. I say the three names back to you so that all three are kept: Says-It-Plain, Hides-In-Reeds, Keeps-The-Old-Count. The heirs will take the last two back to the Rose. I will not tell you that costs nothing.
Ask Tsaxi, not me, what the heirs hold against each of them. I would not say it for him.
Hides-In-Reeds goes. I hold the three names: Hides-In-Reeds, Says-It-Plain, Keeps-The-Old-Count. The heirs will take the other two back to the Rose.
I cannot call what you did clean or foul. I have kept all three names.
Keeps-The-Old-Count goes. Her name first, then Says-It-Plain and Hides-In-Reeds. I keep all three. The heirs will take those two back to the Rose.
I will see that what the heirs reckon she owes is never put on Rows-For-Another, her daughter. I give you that as my own promise.
Says-It-Plain is out of the heirs' reach. Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count are still held. The heirs will take them back to the Rose. I keep the cost of it.
Hides-In-Reeds is beyond the heirs now. Says-It-Plain and Keeps-The-Old-Count are still held. They will go back to the Rose. I keep all three names.
Keeps-The-Old-Count is clear of the heirs. What they reckon she owes will not fall on her daughter. Says-It-Plain and Hides-In-Reeds are still held. Their names stay with me.

infos.prompt: Why do the heirs hold you?
lines: I said it in the Rose's hall, to the families' faces. A ledger kept by families born owing is the Blackguards' ledger kept again.
Under native law, words cost nothing. The heirs reckoned me a season for them all the same, so I stand here at their post.
I say things plainly. I know I say them too plainly. The other two have heard me do it often enough. I would say it again.
Then I go once his back is turned. He lets me go because it suits him. It is not just, and I will not thank him for it.
Say my name to Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house: Says-It-Plain. I want it spoken aloud there, so that it is not lost.
The other two stay. I do not pretend I like that. Go back north-west through the town to her house.

Go back north-west through the town to her house. Do not let my name go quiet.
One of us has gone from here. I am still held. I do not blame you for that.

infos.prompt: Who are you, and who are these three?
lines: I am Third-Born Tsaxi, one of the heirs. The heirs keep this post on the shore. I keep the count of those held here. Outsiders call the Rose a prison. We were born there. What is owed there is how the heirs keep order.

After the fire, three of our held were brought here to the post, a man and two women. Each of them will give you a name and tell you why the heirs hold them. Speak to them where they stand. For the fire itself, ask Never-Sold.

lines: Coin first. I need a hundred in my hand before we talk of the count. Until I have it, I will not speak of one head short.

Says-It-Plain, then. I will turn my back while he goes. I will tell the heirs he died in the smoke. The other two stay held here, as the heirs ordered. The heirs were angry at his words. I will not say they had no cause.

Hides-In-Reeds, then. The heirs will take that hard. I will carry it. When they come to count, I will say she died in the smoke. I will not look when she goes. Says-It-Plain and Keeps-The-Old-Count I keep.

Keeps-The-Old-Count, then. She is old. The heirs will believe the smoke was too much for her. I will not watch the door when she goes. The other two stay held here, and I will not speak of what the heirs reckon for her daughter.
